claims.text: The driver's own GPS trace measures 5.63 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against a platform optimal of 3.1 km — an excess of 2.53 km, or 81.6% of optimal. Both establishment gates in POL-RD-01 are passed (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute), and because the excess also exceeds 50% this is additionally a MATERIAL deviation on this trip's own trace.

POL-RD-01 provides expressly that where the two distance fields disagree, gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs and trip_record.actual_distance_km may NOT be cited for the threshold test. The trace figure 5.63 km is therefore the number the tribunal must work from, not the rounded 5.6 km convenience copy.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes. It carries 121 fixes at a 10 second cadence with coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec of 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a) (gap over 90 s), (b) (jump over 500 m) or (c) (sampling interval above 30 s) is met. The deviation may therefore be established on the trace alone, without the independent corroboration POL-RD-07(ii) demands of an impaired trace.

No traffic advisory exists in this pool: EV-ADVIS-00520-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload. No advisory names any road or segment of this corridor, so no part of the excess can be exonerated under POL-RD-03, and the absence of the artifact is itself citable. The driver cannot attribute this trip's 2.53 km of excess to a closure.

The rider does not dispute the instruction: the chat log records the rider asking at 11:37:10, thirty seconds after the vehicle started at 11:36:40, to stop at Sheng Siong 'first', and the platform resolved a waypoint_hint for that message. That instruction is on the record. But POL-RD-04 exonerates only 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor', and the parties invoking an exculpatory clause bear the burden under POL-RD-08 of pointing to the artifact and clause that fixes its quantum — a general assertion that the whole 2.53 km was the requested stop does not discharge it.

POL-RD-04 requires the gps_trace itself to corroborate the detour — the vehicle must pass within 200 m of the requested waypoint, or travel the road named. No artifact in this pool states any proximity figure between the trace and the waypoint_hint coordinate, and the raw fixes have been withheld from the brief so neither advocate nor judge may run that test by hand. The corroboration element is therefore unproven on this record rather than disproven, and the excess attributable to the request cannot be measured from it.

On the record as it stands no exculpatory clause reduces any part of the excess, so POL-RD-01 retains a MATERIAL deviation and POL-RD-02 runs its arithmetic: charged_total is 12.53; recomputed_fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 3.1 + 0.28 x 6.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 8.605; refund = 12.53 - 8.605 = 3.925, which rounds UP to SGD 3.95 payable. The rider's own statement is that the fare 'should have been the same as always', which is exactly the recomputation POL-RD-02 performs.

The rider carries no adverse profile trigger. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 extra-corroboration condition (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) does not fire and this claim needs nothing beyond the trace that already proves it.

POL-RD-06 gives the driver nothing here. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, far below both the 3-flag and the 0.05-ratio limbs, so no repeat pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift is licensed and no conduct referral follows. The driver's rating, lifetime_trips, acceptance_rate and active_region are context only under POL-GEN-01 and may ground no finding either way.

If any part of the requested stop is allowed to exonerate the excess, the driver's own compensation limb is bounded by the trace rather than by his assertion: the shortfall between the billed 3.1 km and the trace's 5.63 km is 2.53 km, which at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre is 1.8975 and rounds UP to SGD 1.90. That figure is a ceiling, not a floor, and the 2.4 km stated in the claim text appears nowhere in the record.

The fare carries no ERP gantries (erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp 0.0) and no airport or other fixed surcharge, so POL-RD-09 yields no pass-through correction for either party and the money genuinely in issue is confined to the distance and time lines of the fare breakdown. There is no hidden line the driver can recover behind.

Every artifact that carries a deciding fact here — the GPS trace and the fare breakdown — carries weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence cap in POL-GEN-02(2) does not bite and no automatic POL-RD-10(1) escalation arises from evidence weights. The only zero-weight artifact is the absent advisory, which carries no fact and is cited only for its absence under POL-GEN-02(3).

claims.text: The stop was the rider's own idea, recorded in the platform's chat log: MSG-00520-001, sent by sender RIDER at 11:37:10, reads 'can stop at Sheng Siong Blk 501 first? need to grab something', and the trip started at 11:36:40 — so the instruction preceded any departure from the optimal corridor and was given barely 30 seconds into the trip. POL-RD-04(a) and POL-RD-04(b) are satisfied on the face of the log.

The instruction names a specific, actionable place — 'Sheng Siong Blk 501' — and the platform resolved it to a waypoint at ingest (waypoint_hint 1.3549, 103.9458 carried on MSG-00520-001). The POL-RD-04 corroboration test is therefore a field comparison on this record and not an act of geocoding, and the driver's reply 'ok' at 11:37:30 accepts the requested stop.

The trace corroborates a detour of exactly the size the stop would produce: the driver covered 5.63 km against a booked optimal of 3.1 km, an excess of 2.53 km or 81.6% over optimal, and the recorded speed profile runs at 0.0 and 8.4–11.9 km/h through the local-road and stationary stretch before resuming at 23–26.5 km/h — the signature of leaving the corridor for a stop and rejoining it.

Because the whole of that excess is attributable to the rider's recorded instruction, POL-RD-04 excludes it before POL-RD-01 is applied. The excess remaining after exclusion is nil, so neither the 0.8 km absolute gate nor the 20% gate in POL-RD-01 is met; no deviation is established and no rider refund under POL-RD-02 arises.

The fare ledger is the mirror image of the driver's complaint: it charges the rider for 3.1 km of distance while the trace records 5.63 km, so 2.53 km was driven and never billed. That shortfall exceeds the 1.0 km threshold in the compensation limb of POL-RD-04, and at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre the driver is owed 2.53 x 0.75 = SGD 1.8975, rounded up to SGD 1.90, comfortably inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap.

The rider's own counterstatement removes any factual dispute that the detour was requested — 'I did ask him to stop at the supermarket, that is true' — which matches MSG-00520-001 in the chat export. Her objection is to paying more, not to whether the stop was asked for or made.

No closure exoneration can compete with this account: EV-ADVIS-00520-01 is a MISSING traffic advisory (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0), so no advisory covers the optimal corridor and POL-RD-03 supplies no alternative cause for the 2.53 km. The rider-requested stop stands as the only supported explanation, which is what carries the compensation limb of POL-RD-04 rather than the closure limb of POL-RD-03.

There is no repeat-deviation case against the driver to weigh the other way: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so the POL-RD-06 pattern test does not fire, no FULL_REFUND uplift applies and no driver-conduct referral is warranted on this record.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — this resolves the dispute over trip TRP-00520.

What the record shows. The in-app chat (EV-CHAT-00520) records the rider asking at 11:37:10 — thirty seconds after the trip started at 11:36:40 — 'can stop at Sheng Siong Blk 501 first? need to grab something', with the platform's resolved waypoint for Sheng Siong Supermarket Blk 501 Tampines Central 1, and the driver replying 'ok' at 11:37:30. The rider confirms the request in her own statement: 'I did ask him to stop at the supermarket, that is true.'

The deviation. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00520) records 5.63 km — trace_distance_km, which governs over the trip record's rounded 5.6 km actual_distance_km — against the booked optimal of 3.1 km, an excess of 2.53 km or 81.6%, which would pass both POL-RD-01 gates and be MATERIAL. But that extra distance was requested by the rider, so POL-RD-04 excludes it: no deviation is established and no distance refund arises for the rider under POL-RD-02. Her position that the fare 'should have been the same as always' does not by itself create a refund, because the detour was hers to request. Her point that the 200 m waypoint corroboration could not be run is noted but not decisive: the clause's own unavailability test (a null waypoint_hint) is not met, and the detour is confirmed by her own admission and the trace's extra distance and stationary/slow-speed stretch.

The unbilled distance. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00520) billed the rider for only 3.1 km of distance while the trace records 5.63 km. 5.63 − 3.1 = 2.53 km was driven and never billed. That exceeds the 1.0 km threshold in POL-RD-04's compensation limb, so the driver is owed SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 2.53 × 0.75 = SGD 1.8975, rounded up to SGD 1.90, well inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. The 2.4 km figure in the driver's narrative is not used; the record supports 2.53 km.

Other points. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes (121 fixes, 10 s cadence, max_gap_sec 0.0), so POL-RD-07 does not displace the trace-based finding and no independent corroboration is required. No repeat-deviation pattern arises (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 250 completed trips), so no POL-RD-06 conduct referral is made. There are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines, so POL-RD-09 yields no correction. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00520-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT): it carries no fact and only means no road-closure exoneration is available. Profile fields such as rating, lifetime trips, acceptance rate and active region are context only under POL-GEN-01 and ground no finding either way.

Confidence. The deciding unbilled-distance figure is carried by the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, both at weight 1.0, so no weight cap presses confidence below 0.85. The money the ruling moves is SGD 1.90, paid to the driver; both amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd carry that same figure and no second payment or rider refund is created.

Both of you: this is about trip TRP-00520 on 8 Sep 2026, Tampines to Pasir Ris.

The measurements. The platform's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-00520, weight 1.0) records 5.63 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff; the booked optimal is 3.1 km (EV-TRIP-00520), an excess of 2.53 km (81.6%). The trace is clean — 121 fixes at 10 s cadence, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, coverage 100% — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), and the deviation may be read from it.

The rider-requested stop. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00520, weight 1.0) records the rider asking at 11:37:10, thirty seconds after the trip started, 'can stop at Sheng Siong Blk 501 first? need to grab something', with a waypoint_hint resolved at ingest, and the driver replying 'ok'. The rider's own statement — 'I did ask him to stop at the supermarket, that is true' — is an admission against her interest and confirms the request. The trace corroborates the detour: the 2.53 km of excess, with the speed profile running at 0.0 and 8.4-11.9 km/h through a local-road and stationary stretch before resuming at 23-26.5 km/h, is the signature of leaving the corridor for a stop and rejoining it. POL-RD-04 therefore excludes the excess before POL-RD-01 is applied, and no deviation is established. The rider's argument that the 200 m proximity test cannot be run is rejected: POL-RD-04 makes the clause unavailable only where waypoint_hint is null, and here that field is present and non-null, carried on the message itself.

What that means for the fare. Because no deviation survives, POL-RD-02 does not run and the 3.95 recomputation the rider's advocate proposed (charged_total 12.53 less a recomputed_fare of 8.605) is not paid — that is the number that would follow only if the rider's own requested stop were charged back to the driver. No pass-through correction arises either: erp_gantries is empty and tolls_erp is 0.0 on EV-FARE-00520, so POL-RD-09 yields nothing to either party.

The driver's compensation. Separately, POL-RD-04 compensates the driver where the fare billed less distance than the trace records and the shortfall exceeds 1.0 km. The fare billed 3.1 km (distance_charged_km) while the trace records 5.63 km — a shortfall of 2.53 km. The requested stop therefore accounts for the detour. No closure competes with it: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00520-01 is absent (status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 supplies no alternative cause. The money. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00520) charged distance on only the booked 3.1 km (distance_charged_km 3.1; charged_total 12.53), so 2.53 km actually driven was never billed. POL-RD-04's compensation limb applies where the billed distance falls short of the trace distance by more than 1.0 km: 5.63 - 3.1 = 2.53 unbilled km, at SGD 0.75 per unbilled km = 1.8975, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 1.90, well inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. The excess attributable to the rider's own stop is excluded before POL-RD-01 is applied, so no deviation is established against the driver and no distance refund is due to the rider; the rider's recomputation figures of 3.925, rounded to SGD 3.95, are therefore not payable.

Driver compensation. Separately, POL-RD-04 pays the driver for distance the fare did not bill. The shortfall is 2.53 km, above the 1.0 km threshold, and 2.53 × SGD 0.75 = SGD 1.8975, rounded UP to SGD 1.90 — within the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap and exactly the SGD 1.90 the driver claimed.
